incident_spec.summary: High percentage of temporary tables created on disk in MySQL.
symptoms: 30% of temporary tables created on disk.
Observed reduction in disk-based temporary tables after increasing `tmp_table_size` and `max_heap_table_size`.
Another system with the same database shows only 1% disk-based temporary tables.
incident_spec.mechanism: MySQL creates temporary tables on disk when certain conditions are met, such as the presence of TEXT/BLOB fields, exceeding memory limits for temporary tables, or using large columns with GROUP BY, UNION, or ORDER BY.

facts.evidence: The DBA explicitly mentioned increasing these settings to reduce disk-based temporary tables.

facts.key: 30% of temporary tables created on disk
facts.evidence: The DBA reported this statistic from MySQL Tuner.

facts.key: TEXT/BLOB fields lead to disk-based temporary tables
facts.evidence: The answer mentions that TEXT/BLOB fields cannot be handled by MEMORY tables.

facts.key: Another system with the same database shows 1% disk-based temporary tables
facts.evidence: The DBA compared the problematic system with another system.

assumptions: The problematic queries involve GROUP BY, UNION, or ORDER BY with large columns or TEXT/BLOB fields.
The database schema includes TEXT/BLOB fields or large VARCHAR columns.
unknowns: The exact schema of the database.
The specific queries causing the issue.
Whether the workload differs between the two systems.
